sarah (EvalOps): FYI nightly eval flagged a quality regression on model-3.4-quant around prefix-handling. failing rate jumped ~12% on the concierge prompt set :warning:
ci-bot: nightly-eval report: https://ci.internal/reports/2026-03-... (summary attached) :page_with_curl:

sarah (EvalOps): example failure: generation truncated mid-entity and sometimes repeats prefix when the input shares a short common prefix. here's one of the bad gens we captured:
```
PROMPT: "Customer: My subscription auto-renews on 4/1. Will I be charged if I cancel now?"
EXPECTED: contains clear billing policy steps and refund window
ACTUAL: "Customer: My subscription auto-renews on 4/1. Will I be charged if I cancel now? My subscription... My subscription..."
```

arjun (AppliedML): interesting. did this start after the prefix cache rollout from last week? @tomas any changes to cache key logic? :eyes:

tomas (Runtime): we rolled a change that shortens cache keys to 64 bytes to reduce index size. quick note: the key now uses first N bytes of prefix + model id + quant flag. iirc it accidentally drops the length-salt for prefixes > 64 bytes. could cause collisions when two different prefixes share the same first 64 bytes. investigating.

maya (ML Eng): I can repro locally with a small harness. two different user prompts that share a 64-byte common prefix produce identical cache hits and identical KV cache used for generation => determinism broken. repro script I used:
```bash
# send two prompts that differ after 64 bytes
python eval_harness/run_prompt.py --model model-3.4-quant --prompt-file examples/prefixA.txt
python eval_harness/run_prompt.py --model model-3.4-quant --prompt-file examples/prefixB.txt
# compare outputs
diff outputs/prefixA.out outputs/prefixB.out || true
```

arjun (AppliedML): can you paste the two prefixes (sanitized) so we can confirm collision?

maya (ML Eng): pasted below (shortened to show collision area):
```
PREFIX_A= "Order id: 8a3f... [64 bytes total] then rest A..."
PREFIX_B= "Order id: 8a3f... [same 64 bytes] then rest B..."
```
Both produced the same continuation initially.

sarah (EvalOps): correlate with nightly eval failures: most affected prompts are templated system messages (billing/legal templates) that share long identical headers. The eval set includes many such templates => explains spike.

ci-bot: deploy #runt-2026.03.10-2 completed. change: cache-key-compactification (author: t.runtime)

arjun (AppliedML): OK this sounds like a textbook prefix cache collision. mitigation options:
- roll back compact keys (restore length-salt) :thumbsup:
- add stronger hash (sha256) to key, maybe truncated but with salt :wrench:
- disable prefix caching for templated prompts until fixed :no_entry:
Which is fastest?

tomas (Runtime): fastest is feature-flagging prefix cache off for affected model family and region. rolling full rollback is heavier. I can push a feature flag in ~30m. Also pushing a patch to include a 4-byte length suffix to the key; that should be safe and cheap.

maya (ML Eng): temporary test: setting REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE=false on dev reproduced golden behaviour (no collision). can add an integration test to nightly eval harness to assert uniqueness of cache keys for different prompts.

arjun (AppliedML): can we add a unit test too that constructs two long prefixes differing after 64 bytes and assert cache_key(prefixA) != cache_key(prefixB)? put it in runtime/cache/tests.

maya (ML Eng): will do. also adding a targeted eval check to flag increased identical-generation rates for templated clusters.

sarah (EvalOps): I'll mute the noisy alert for the specific check and open a regression ticket with examples so SRE / CS don't get paged repeatedly. ticket: INF-4521

ci-bot: created ticket INF-4521: "prefix-cache collisions causing hallucination-like repeats" assigned to runtime team

tomas (Runtime): deploying feature-flag OFF for prefix cache on production fleet for model-3.4-quant now. will monitor token-per-second and latency impact.

arjun (AppliedML): thanks. action items:
- tomas: feature-flag disable + length-suffix patch (in prod)
- maya: unit test + eval test + repro script committed
- sarah: attach failing prompt list to INF-4521 and update regression dashboard

maya (ML Eng): patch PR: runtime#1289 includes 4-byte length suffix and new unit tests. small perf hit on key generation but negligible.

sarah (EvalOps): after disabling prefix cache, nightly rerun looks much better — failing rate down to baseline. will leave the regression job unmuted and monitor for 48h. :white_check_mark:

arjun (AppliedML): great triage. let's also create a postmortem-ish note for eng docs on "cache-key safety" and the eval impact so future changes have a checklist.

ci-bot: nightly-eval rerun (2026-03-10T08:00Z): failure rate back to baseline. report: https://ci.internal/reports/2026-03-10-rerun

tomas (Runtime): follow-up: I'll roll the length-suffix as the default and add a config flag to choose hash function. will also add instrumentation to log when two different prefixes map to same key (sampling only).

sarah (EvalOps): adding a monitoring alert: if identical-generation-rate for templated clusters increases by >5% over 3 runs, page oncall.

arjun (AppliedML): thanks team. tagging this resolved for now; will keep INF-4521 open until we see stable postfix. :v:
